subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should OpenClaw add recurring native PowerShell smoke coverage for check:docs, build:strict-smoke, or a narrower first command set in the existing Windows CI lane?
rationale: The request fits test-infrastructure priorities, but it changes recurring Windows CI scope and the active candidate currently proves one selected command is not safe in the target lane.

options.title: Land after passing full smoke
options.body: Keep the requested command set, but merge only after the exact Windows pwsh lane passes and the PR includes redacted successful proof.

options.title: Start narrower
options.body: Limit the first smoke lane to commands that already pass under native PowerShell, then track build-smoke coverage separately.

options.title: Defer recurring coverage
options.body: Keep the issue open but do not add a recurring Windows smoke step until runner budget or release priorities justify it.

recommendation.title: Land after passing full smoke
recommendation.body: Keep the requested command set, but merge only after the exact Windows pwsh lane passes and the PR includes redacted successful proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest recent overlap across CI workflow stabilization and PowerShell-safe docs tooling.
